name: secure sampling protocols benchmark
description: Differential privacy (DP) is widely employed to provide privacy protection for individuals by limiting information leakage from the aggregated data. Two well-known models of DP are the central model and the local model. The former requires a trustworthy server for data aggregation, while the latter requires individuals to add noise, significantly decreasing the utility of aggregated results. Recently, many studies have proposed to achieve DP with Secure Multi-party Computation (MPC) in distributed settings, namely, the distributed model, which has utility comparable to central model while, under specific security assumptions, preventing parties from obtaining others' information. One challenge of realizing DP in distributed model is efficiently sampling noise with MPC. Although many secure sampling methods have been proposed, they have different security assumptions and isolated theoretical analyses. There is a lack of experimental evaluations to measure and compare their performances.
evaluation_method: runtime/efficiency comparison and empirical utility/privacy tradeoff analysis
reputation: A niche research benchmark for comparing secure MPC-based DP sampling protocols; mainly of interest to privacy and cryptography researchers.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; focuses on experimental comparison of secure sampling methods rather than a fixed accuracy-style score.
